pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-02.png with Read and looked at it before reading any other document. It is a placeholder storyboard: grey boxes with name labels, no art. Panel 1 (wide, top): I read the white caption at top left first, 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.', then the teal label at top right, 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'. Ananya's box is centre-left. No one speaks. Panel 2 (middle left): Ananya says 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' The tail points right and down to her. Panel 3 (middle right, narrow): Meera says 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' The tail points down to her. Below that is the teal label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'. Panel 4 (wide, bottom): Ananya's box is left of centre and Meera's is right. The balloon 'One team. Better coordination.' sits between them, and a very short tail points left to Ananya. Meera has no line.
pages.observation: 1) Panel 4: the balloon sits between Ananya and Meera and covers the end of the 'ananya' label. Its tail is only a few pixels long, so a reader could easily give 'One team. Better coordination.' to Meera, who is just to its right. Move the balloon or lengthen the tail clearly toward Ananya. 2) Panels 2 to 3: Meera's 'And our team...' finishes Ananya's thought, and it read naturally left to right. 3) The teal boxes are a different style from the white caption. I could not tell whether they are narration, signage or product labels. 4) The roles of Ananya and Meera (doctor? receptionist?) are not shown anywhere on this page. 5) Panel 1 is large and mostly empty, so I cannot judge the establishing shot from this placeholder.

pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.png with Read and looked at it. Panel 1 (top left, large): Ravi's box is upper right and Meera's is lower left. The balloon at top left, 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.', has a tail pointing right to Ravi. Panel 2 (top right, narrow): Ravi's box is small on the left and Meera's is to his right. Meera says 'Of course. May I register your details for today's appointment?' with the tail pointing down to her. Panel 3 (wide, middle): Ravi is left and Meera is right. Ravi says 'Yes, please.' from a balloon at top left. Panel 4 (wide, bottom): Ravi is left and Meera is right. Meera says 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' with the tail pointing down-right to her. All four lines read in the order intended.
pages.observation: 1) The characters swap sides. In panel 1 Ravi is right and Meera left; in panels 2 to 4 Ravi is left and Meera right. With no art showing a camera change, this reads as a jump across the line. Either keep the same sides or show the turn clearly. 2) Registration happens between panel 3 ('Yes, please.') and panel 4 ('You're all set') and is never shown. Panel 3 is a wide panel holding only two words, so it could show the registration action, such as a tablet or form. 3) In panel 1 Ravi only asks to see the doctor, but Meera then says 'today's appointment'. It is unclear whether he already had an appointment. 4) Meera's use of 'Ravi' is acceptable after registration. 5) Nothing on this page sets the location or time. The reception setting can only be guessed from the dialogue.

pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png with Read and looked at it. Panel 1 (wide, top): Ananya is left and Ravi right. Ananya says 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' The balloon sits right of her box and covers part of her label. Panel 2 (middle left): Ravi's box is centre-right. Ananya appears only as a label dot at the far left, with no box. Ravi says 'I've been feeling tired lately.' Panel 3 (middle right): a white narration box at the top reads 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' Ananya's box is centre. Ravi appears only as a dot at the far right edge. Panel 4 (wide, bottom): Ananya is left and Ravi right. Ananya says 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' The balloon covers her label.
pages.observation: 1) There is no caption or establishing cue for the move from reception (page 3) to the consultation. Ananya is identifiable as 'the doctor' only by inference from Ravi's request on page 3. 2) Ananya and Ravi keep the same sides across all four panels, which helps continuity. 3) The narration in panel 3 comes between Ravi's symptom and Ananya's reply. Her reply, 'We'll go through your concerns...', is generic and does not answer 'tired' directly, so the exchange feels thin. 4) The caption names 'Technology', but no device is indicated in the panel. I cannot tell what technology is meant. 5) In panels 1 and 4 the balloons and tails sit on top of Ananya's name label. Her mouth or face position may be covered and should be checked in later art.

pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png with Read and looked at it. Panel 1 (wide, top): Meera is centre-left and Ravi right. Meera says 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' The balloon is at left with its tail pointing right to her. Panel 2 (middle left): Ravi says 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' with a short tail pointing right to his box. The teal label 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients' is at bottom left. Panel 3 (middle right): Meera says 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' with the tail pointing down to her. Ravi appears only as a dot at the far right edge, and his label crosses the panel border. Panel 4 (wide, bottom): the white caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' is at the top. Ananya and Meera are small, side by side, left of centre. Ravi is on the right. Ravi speaks no line in panel 4.
pages.observation: 1) The scene changes from Ananya's consultation (page 4) back to Meera without any time or place cue. A reader cannot tell whether this happens after the consultation or where. 2) Ravi's 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' starts with 'So', as if he were inferring from Meera's line. But Meera spoke about staying 'connected with their care', not about information in one place, so the logical step feels skipped. 3) In panel 2 the teal label appears after Ravi's question, which reads naturally as a product tag. 4) In panel 3 Ravi's marker and label cross the right border. 5) In panel 4 Ananya's label is cut to 'anany' by Meera's box. It is unclear what is happening in that panel: Ravi leaving, or all three together. The caption reads as advertising narration, not story.

pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-06.png with Read and looked at it. Panel 1 (top left): the white caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' sits beside Ravi's box. Panel 2 (top right): the teal label 'WELBUK VISION' is at top left, the specialist's box is upper right, and the white caption at the bottom reads 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' Panel 3 (wide, middle): the teal label 'WELBUK VISION' appears again, followed by the white caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' Ravi, a partner and a child are to the right. Panel 4 (large, bottom): Meera, Ananya and Ravi stand in a row; Ravi's label is cut to 'rav' by the teal box. The teal box at top right reads 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health', and the white caption at bottom left reads 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' The page has no spoken dialogue.
pages.observation: 1) 'Tomorrow' is ambiguous: it could mean the literal next day or the future. 'us' and 'our hometown' have no clear speaker. Because the caption sits beside Ravi, it could be read as his inner voice or as a narrator. 2) The partner and the child appear here for the first time on pages 2 to 6, with no introduction. 3) The specialist's location ('beyond our hometown', 'across locations') is not shown. 4) The 'WELBUK VISION' label is repeated in panels 2 and 3, which feels redundant. 5) In panel 4 I read the teal product list (top right) before the bottom-left caption. That order works, but the teal box covers Ravi's label and possibly his face area. 6) The whole page is captions and product labels with no dialogue. It reads as an advertisement ending, not a story beat for the characters.
